hints: Two things change: the number of squares and their color.
Count the squares: 1, 2, 3, 4. Then look at the colors: black, white, black, white.
The count goes up by 1, and the color switches each time. Find the next count, then the next color.

solution.methodName: Check one change at a time

steps.action: Count the squares: 1, 2, 3, 4. The count goes up by 1, so the next figure has 5 squares.
Check the colors: black (■), white (□), black, white. The color switches every time, so the next figure is black.
steps.why: Check one change at a time. Count first, then color, so you don't mix them up.

steps.action: Put both together: 5 black squares. The answer is ■■■■■.

trapNotes.□□□□□: This has the right count but the wrong color. The colors switch: after white (□□□□) comes black.
trapNotes.■■■■: This has the right color but only 4 squares. The count goes up by 1 each time, so the next figure has 5.
trapNotes.■■■■■■: This has 6 squares, adding 2 instead of 1. The count goes 1, 2, 3, 4, so next is 5.
